Hi Sebastian — appreciate the clear ask.

Short answer up front: we recommend an active-in-region, cold-standby cross-region failover for regulated countries by default, with options for warm-standby replication for teams willing to accept limited cross-border replication of encrypted KV snapshots.

I'll put together a one-page proposal and loop in our infra and security leads for the technical & compliance details. Expect a follow-up in ~3 business days with diagrams and a proposed RTO/RPO.

Two quick clarifying Qs from our side to tailor the proposal:
1) Are you OK with encrypted-at-rest snapshots being replicated only upon failover, or must there be zero cross-border transmission at any time?
2) Do you need model artifacts (weights/cache) also restricted to-country, or are those acceptable to host in a regional (EU or APAC) bucket?

Thanks — DL

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Sebastian Meyer <sebastian.meyer@acme-int.eu>, jenny.lam@acme-apac.com
Date: 2026-11-04T14:00:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Region boundary and failover for private deployments — Acme request

Dylan / team / Sebastian — drafted the technical proposal below (high-level). I've attached an updated network diagram.

Proposal (high-level):
- Residency model: per-country regional control plane + compute isolated to the customer's VPC in-region. Persistent customer data (logs, request history, KV cache snapshots) are stored in region-bound object stores and encrypted with a customer or tenant-specific KMS key located in-region.

- Failover model: default configuration = active-in-region (active serving in-region). Failover options:
  * Cold standby (default for regulated deployments): encrypted snapshots of KV/cache and model metadata are securely transferred only when failover is triggered (via our runbook). This avoids continuous cross-border replication. RTO target: 2–4 hours depending on model size; RPO: last nightly snapshot.
  * Warm standby (optional): periodic encrypted incremental replication of KV snapshots to a standby region under strict access controls and separate KMS keys. This reduces RTO to 15–60 minutes but requires cross-border replication acceptance.
  * Active-active (not recommended for strict residency): traffic may be routed in-region with global load balancing but requires continuous cross-border data flow/consistency guarantees which many regulated customers do not accept.

- Network considerations:
  * Private endpoints into the customer's VPC (VPC peering or transit gateway) — we avoid public internet egress for data paths.
  * BGP health checks and automated route withdrawal to trigger failover at the network layer.
  * Egress minimization: model weights and cold storage kept in-region. If snapshots cross borders on failover, transfers are encrypted (TLS1.3 + IPsec option) and logged.

- Key management and encryption:
  * Option A — customer-managed KMS in-region: Redwood integrates to the customer's KMS so keys never leave jurisdiction.
  * Option B — Redwood-managed KMS with regional HSM-backed keys and strict access controls; separate keys per jurisdiction.

- Logging & audit:
  * Request traces and audit logs stored in-region. Cross-region retention copies only created on explicit failover events.
  * We can provide sample audit extracts (IP ranges, transfer manifests) as part of evidence pack.

- Operational runbooks:
  * Failover runbook (trigger ops, validation checks, manual approvals for cross-border snapshot restore)
  * Reversibility plan (ensure data deletion in standby after failback)

Next steps / open items:
1) Confirm whether Acme requires zero cross-border transmission at any time (this forces cold-standby only).
2) If warm standby is acceptable, define acceptable RTO/RPO and who holds keys.
3) Schedule 30-min sync Friday for walkthrough of the diagram.

Attachment: net-diagram-acme-v1-updated.png

Happy to expand any section. Marcus — can you add the storage/replication cost estimates? Vivek — can you confirm the automation hooks we expose for runbook triggers.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sebastian / team — quick compliance summary and recommended artifacts we can provide for your GRC pack: 

What we can deliver now:
- Network diagram (in-region endpoints, BGP failover notes) — attached.
- Technical proposal (one-pager) that codifies active-in-region + cold/warm standby options.
- DPA comments: we can accept Acme's draft with a small amendment clarifying emergency cross-border transfer procedures (would include explicit triggers and retention/deletion requirements).
- KMS options: we support customer-managed keys in-region (preferred for regulated customers).
- Evidence pointers: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), sample audit extracts (transfer manifests), and runbook excerpts.

Open compliance questions:
1) Jurisdictional requirement granularity — do you need per-country (e.g., AU state-level) or per-region (APAC) controls?
2) Data subject request flows — do you require Redwood to delete request traces immediately upon a DSAR, or is a joint process with Acme acceptable?

Proposed next steps:
- We will produce the one-page proposal + updated diagram and a short list of deliverables by EOD tomorrow.
- If helpful, sign a short NDA addendum for the topology diagrams; otherwise we can provide redacted versions for vendor reviews.

We'll await Acme's answers to the two compliance questions to finalize the recommended configuration. Happy to jump on the Friday sync.

Best,
Laura Bennett
